hero.title: BBA in Finland
hero.subtitle: Experience world-class academic training and global career pathways in Finland with Edu-Hawk Worldwide.

overview: International students can explore English-taught Bachelor of Business Administration in Finland programmes, particularly in International Business and related fields. These degrees help students develop business communication, analytical thinking, leadership and problem-solving skills for an increasingly global job market.

faq.question: How long does it take to complete a BBA in Finland?
faq.answer: A typical Bachelor of Business Administration at a Finnish university of applied sciences takes approximately 3.5 years and consists of 210 ECTS credits. The exact duration depends on the programme and study plan.

faq.question: What is the BBA fee in Finland for Indian students?
faq.answer: For the selected programmes in this guide, Haaga-Helia lists €11,000 per year for applicable non-EU/EEA students, approximately ₹11.95 lakh. The University of Oulu lists €10,000 per year for its bachelor’s phase in International Business Management, approximately ₹10.86 lakh. Fees can change and are separate from living expenses.

faq.question: Can I study BBA in Finland in English?
faq.answer: Yes. Institutions such as Haaga-Helia offer English-taught business programmes. Always confirm the language of instruction and the availability of the programme for your intended intake.

faq.question: What are the eligibility requirements for BBA in Finland after Class 12?
faq.answer: Applicants generally need a recognised secondary-school qualification equivalent to the university’s entry requirements. Depending on the programme, they may also need proof of English proficiency, SAT results or another approved selection assessment.

faq.question: Can I work in Finland after completing a BBA?
faq.answer: Graduates can explore relevant employment opportunities, subject to employer requirements and the immigration rules in force. Job availability and outcomes depend on skills, experience, language proficiency and the local employment market.
